handoff: All ACs tested and green, but 3 blocking store bugs: hash-object applies autocrlf/filters so recordTreeId != packed tree (push_record every tick, record not byte-faithful); unpack trusts '..' tree paths; unpack merges into existing dest instead of replacing (D3).

findings.title: hash-object applies filters (autocrlf, clean filters), so the packed tree differs from recordTreeId and from the files
findings.detail:
`git hash-object -w --stdin-paths` runs the user's conversion (core.autocrlf, global attributes such as filter=lfs). recordTreeId hashes the raw bytes. Repro: with `core.autocrlf=input` (set globally on this machine), a run-state file containing `x\r\n` gives recordTreeId a43d0d33… but pushRecord's tree 4d593e93…. A random-tree property check (scratchpad tree-prop.ts) mismatched in 55/60 runs with CRLF content and 0/60 without it. With GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null they match. The consequences: the pushed record is not 'the story's run-state folder as it is in the machine dir' (D2), so an unpack restores altered bytes. Also, observe's tree never equals pushed.tree, so decide emits push_record on every tick for ever (act then returns 'unchanged'), which breaks AC6's 'a boundary whose record tree did not change pushes nothing' at the decision level.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use `hash-object -w --no-filters --stdin-paths` (verified: its id equals the raw `blob N\0…` hash). Add a test with a CRLF file under `-c core.autocrlf=input` (or GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS) asserting recordTreeId == the pushed tree and no push_record on the next tick.

findings.title: unpackRecord trusts tree paths: a `..` entry writes outside the staging folder
findings.detail:
Each `ls-tree -r` path is joined onto staging unchecked (`join(staging, path)`, then mkdirSync and writeFileSync). `git mktree` accepts an entry named `..` (verified: `printf '040000 tree <t>\t..\n' | git mktree` succeeds), and receive.fsckObjects is off by default. So a record ref pushed by another checkout can place files in dest's parent or above, outside the machine dir. Unpack reads refs written by other machines (gh-195/10, /12), so it must not trust them. A path containing a tab is also cut short by `split("\t")`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Reject (return ok:false with an error) any entry with an empty, `.` or `..` component, or whose resolved path is not inside staging. Split only on the first tab. Add a test with a mktree'd `..` entry.

findings.title: unpack merges into an existing dest instead of replacing it
findings.detail:
D3: 'Unpack extracts into a temp folder, validates every JSON file against the schema (S2), then renames into place.' atomicCopyDir (fsx.ts:108-109) first copies the existing `dest` into its temp folder and then lays the staging files over it. Files the record does not hold (extra NNNN-*.json receipts, an older round's state) survive. The result is a mix that was never validated as a whole, and it is not the record.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Rename the validated staging folder into place, replacing dest (move the old one aside, then drop it), without merging. Test it by unpacking over a dest that holds an extra receipt.

findings.title: A stale lease fails every tick, with nothing shown to a person
findings.detail:
fetchNornRefs (store git.ts:188) does not fetch refs/norn/runs/*, so `expected` is only this checkout's own last push. Once another checkout has pushed the ref, every tick tries once and fails as stale. This is one attempt per tick, not a tight loop, and D2's 'never overwrite each other' holds (the AC6 test). But recordFailure skips push_record and nothing reaches the inbox. The implementer noted it as a known limit for the takeover slices (10-12).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Acceptable for this slice if 10-12 own it. Confirm that they surface a stale record push (a Check item) rather than retrying silently.

findings.title: The record is pushed when this tick's branch push failed
findings.detail:
push_record runs regardless of the branch push's result. Norn-Branch-Commit then names the old remote-tracking head, while the packed state.json describes work that is not on the remote. B10 says 'right after the branch push'. `.catch(() => null)` also drops the trailer silently when the tracking ref is missing.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Skip push_record (it stays owed) when the story's branch push failed this tick, or document why a record ahead of its branch is fine.

findings.title: 'Every JSON file' is validated: only state, workflow and receipts are
findings.detail:
The module comment and D3 say every JSON file is validated. recordErrors checks only state.json, the pinned workflow and the receipts, per top-level unit folder and its rounds. Other JSON files (criteria reports, evidence) and top-level files are not validated. Symlink entries (mode 120000) are written as plain files, and `files: list.length` counts entries that were skipped.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make the comment match the code, or validate the rest. Reject or skip non-100644/100755 blobs explicitly.

findings.title: filesUnder packs transient staging and tmp folders
findings.detail:
Leftover `.x.move-<pid>` (copyTreeRecord) and atomic-copy tmp folders inside the story's run-state folder would be packed and pushed.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Skip dot-prefixed staging and tmp names in filesUnder (and thus in recordTreeId).

findings.title: 'Absent behaves as local' is shown only through config get, never by running a story
findings.detail:
AC1 says 'when a story runs, then it behaves as local'. AC3 runs a story with an explicit `policy: local`, and no story runs with the key absent. resolveConfig defaults to local, and decide falls back to it (`config.record?.policy ?? "local"`, story.ts:138, which is fine for O5 replay of older configs).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optionally run AC3 with policy(null).
